def: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable person, including data that is only linked to someone through other records.
Personally identifiable information, the US term for data that identifies a person, usually narrower than the GDPR's personal data.
The GDPR roles of the party that decides why and how personal data is processed and the party that processes it on the controller's behalf.
The principle of collecting and passing on only the personal data the purpose needs.
Removing a sensitive value from text and leaving only a label, such as [EMAIL_1].
Replacing an identifier with a stand-in that can be mapped back using separately held information, so the data remains personal data.
The principle that data collected for one purpose should not be reused for an incompatible one.
The principle that personal data should be kept no longer than its purpose requires.
A person's right under the GDPR to have their personal data deleted, subject to exceptions such as legal claims.
An obligation to preserve data relevant to a dispute, which can override normal deletion schedules.
A requirement that data be stored, processed or accessed only in certain places, which covers storage, processing and access separately.
A written analysis of the purpose, necessity and risks of high-risk processing, required before launch under GDPR Article 35.
